To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Earth effect in supernova neutrino oscillations is related to the mass hierarchy, that this effect is enhanced for inverted hierarchy and that it may allow us to determine the neutrino mass ordering.
collective flavor transformations in supernovae are enhanced by the presence of Earth matter effects.
collective effects can be present in a galactic supernovae, even if the mixing angle θ13 is small, but only if the mass hierarchy is inverted.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following topics:   1.
the study of neutrino flavor evolution in supernovae and the effects of the Earth matter on the neutrino signal.
the study of the neutrino flavor evolution in dense media.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Earth effects in the antineutrino channel would provide a smoking gun for the inverted mass hierarchy, while the absence of the collective effects in the neutrino channel would indicate the normal hierarchy.
the Earth effects are absent in the antineutrino flux if and only if collective flavor oscillations take place in the supernova.
a supernova neutrino signal can be used to determine the neutrino mass spectrum with a precision better than 1% for θ 13 >10 -4, and with a precision better then 10% for θ 12 >10 -4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a galactic supernovae may be the most promising place to study neutrino mass hierarchy.
the neutrino mass ordering is not only a question of the future but also the question of the past.
, if the neutrino signal from the galactic supernova is observed to be affected by the Earth matter effects, then the neutrino mass ordering must be normal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence (absence) of Earth matter effect in the antineutrino flux is an unambiguous sign of the normal (inverted) mass hierarchy, when θ 13 is extremely small.
a supernova neutrino signal may be used to probe the neutrino mass ordering even when the neutrino mixing angle θ 23 is close to maximal.
a galactic supernovae is a unique probe of the neutrino mass ordering.
